display.purpose: Meeting title on the 1280x720 bot tile.

headline.purpose: Page h1, closed by a 2px ink rule.

label.purpose: Field labels, chips, badges, buttons, tabs; always uppercase.

flap.purpose: One glyph per split-flap cell (md size shown; sm 17px, lg 36px, xl 40px).

shadows.name: cell-edge
shadows.purpose: Lit top edge of a flap cell; removed on a verified cell.

shadows.name: keyline
shadows.purpose: Border drawn inside outlined chips and the waiting badge (ink for the info chip). A line, not depth.

shadows.name: keyline-selected
shadows.purpose: Selected option in the guest pick list.

motion.name: cascade-step
motion.purpose: One intermediate glyph per step in a changing cell; one frame of the 15 fps bot stream. 3 to 5 steps per cell.

motion.name: cascade-stagger
motion.purpose: Delay added per cell, left to right.

motion.name: flap-land
motion.purpose: Each glyph change lands from scaleY(0.25) and brightness(0.55).

motion.name: button-hover
motion.purpose: Button background tint; press is an 80ms 1px translate.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Cascade sets text immediately; landing and button transitions are off.

narrative.overview:
ProveBack looks like the split-flap departure board in a rail station concourse: the one screen every head in the room lifts to. Names and statuses sit in fixed cells on matte board black, lettered in paint white, and a change of status arrives as a mechanical cascade instead of a colour swap. The bot's 1280x720 camera tile is the board itself; the host dashboard and the guest's phone are the working surfaces around it, on a brushed-steel ground, and each of them carries the same board row so a guest's line reads identically wherever it appears.

The system is plain, dense and public-facing. It is a piece of shared signage, so it is legible at a glance, through video compression, in a small tile: large condensed capitals, strong contrast, and a word for every state. It must not read as a crypto project and must not read as a government or border-control system. The interface language is English.

Colour is rationed. The board is black and white; amber means only "this step is happening now"; a dim red marks a row that needs another try; verified is the cell turned over to its white face. There are no gradients, no glow, and no drop shadows.
keyCharacteristics: One shared board row (lamp, 12 name cells, 9 status cells, on board black) on the bot tile, the host's participant list and the guest's phone.
Split-flap cascade as the only signature motion: 66 ms steps, 45 ms stagger, left to right.
Board black and paint white for the board; brushed steel, panel and ink for working screens.
Amber reserved for the step happening now; verified is an inverted paint-white cell, never green.
Every status is a word; colour and lamp only accompany it.
Condensed uppercase for anything the board says; a plain companion sans for sentences, forms and tables.
Flat: no gradients, glow or drop shadows.

rules.name: The Amber Is Now Rule
rules.body: Amber is reserved for the step happening now: a guest who is scanning, a bot that is joining or in the waiting room, a live stream that is reconnecting. It is never decoration, never a brand colour, never a generic warning.

rules.name: The Turned Flap Rule
rules.body: Verified is an inverted cell: paint-white face, board-black letter. It is never green. On light surfaces the same inversion is a board-black badge with paint-white text.

rules.name: The Word First Rule
rules.body: Status is always carried by a word (WAITING, SCANNING, VERIFIED, TRY AGAIN, MEMBER). The lamp and the colour repeat the word; they never replace it. Lamps are hidden from assistive technology and each cell group carries its text for screen readers.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Condensed uppercase is the board speaking; sentence-case Barlow is a person being told something. Never set a sentence in condensed caps, and never set a status word in body type on the board.

rules.name: The Wordmark Rule
rules.body: PROVEBACK is set in Barlow Condensed 700, uppercase, tracked wide (0.18em to 0.3em by size). There is no logo mark.

rules.name: The Flat Board Rule
rules.body: No gradients, no glow, no drop shadows. The only shadow is the cell's inset edge; any other inset value is a keyline standing in for a border.

dos: Do use the shared board row (lamp, 12 name cells, 9 status cells, on board black) whenever a participant's verification state is shown as a line.
Do keep status words to nine characters and uppercase, and pair every lamp and colour with its word.
Do reserve amber for the step happening now.
Do show verified as an inverted paint-white cell on the board and a board-black badge on light surfaces.
Do announce a change of state with the cascade (66 ms steps, 45 ms stagger, left to right) and set the text immediately under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do put a lone Flap on a light surface inside its own strip of board black.
Do disclose a simulation in the first sentence under the heading.
Do design the bot tile for 1280x720 at 15 fps seen small: nothing below 22px, no hover, no scrolling.
Do write the interface in English, in plain sentences.
donts: Don't use green for verified, or any colour as the only carrier of status.
Don't use amber for decoration, branding or generic warnings.
Don't add gradients, glow, blur or drop shadows; the only shadow is the cell's inset edge.
Don't make it look like a crypto project.
Don't make it look like a government, customs or border-control system.
Don't label a simulation with a tag above the heading in place of the sentence under it.
Don't set flap text in proportional widths or mixed case, or let a row change its cell count.
Don't set sentences in condensed capitals.
